definition_tar_lang: Someone more fascinated by side details than the main thing, such as behind-the-scenes trivia, footnotes, map corners, packaging text, or background gossip. They often remember the surrounding fragments better than the actual headline event.
sentence_in_context: 展没认真看，我这个[MASK701]光研究墙上的致谢名单了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I barely looked at the exhibition itself; as a side-detail nerd, I spent all my time studying the acknowledgements list on the wall.
paragraph_in_context: 朋友拉我去看电影首映，我出来先跟他聊片尾彩蛋和海报角落那行小字。主线剧情反而记得一般，演员名字倒背得飞快。可能我真是个[MASK701]，每次都被这些细节勾走注意力。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: A friend dragged me to a movie premiere, and when we came out I immediately started talking about the post-credit easter egg and the tiny line of text in the corner of the poster. I actually only remember the main plot vaguely, but I can rattle off the actors’ names quickly. Maybe I really am a side-detail nerd—these little details steal my attention every time.

definition_tar_lang: A person who compulsively downloads, saves, and stores things in advance in case they later disappear or become unavailable. This includes offline maps, screenshots, duplicate files, and multiple backup versions of the same content.
sentence_in_context: 出门前又把路线截了十张图，我这[MASK702]没救了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Before heading out, I screenshotted the route ten more times—this cache-hoarder side of me is hopeless.
paragraph_in_context: 朋友笑我手机里像个仓库，演唱会门票、聊天记录、旧照片全都不舍得删。昨天只是换个平板，我又连夜备份了三遍。没办法，[MASK702]一到这种时候就特别紧张，总怕哪天突然找不到。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: My friend jokes that my phone is like a warehouse—I can’t bear to delete concert tickets, chat logs, or old photos. Yesterday I was just switching to a new tablet, and I stayed up making three backup copies. I can’t help it: when moments like this come, my cache-hoarder instincts get especially anxious, always afraid something will suddenly be impossible to find one day.

definition_tar_lang: People who spend weekdays borrowing energy from the future and weekends trying unsuccessfully to repay the debt with marathon naps. They use the label jokingly when canceling plans to sleep or waking up still tired after a 'recovery' day.
sentence_in_context: 周末又拒绝聚会了，我这[MASK703]先睡为敬。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I turned down another hangout this weekend—this sleep-debt goblin is going to bed first.
paragraph_in_context: 这周天天加班到快一点，今天本来想出门喝咖啡。结果闹钟一关又睡到中午，朋友喊我也没爬起来。看来我这只[MASK703]，周末计划还是输给枕头了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I worked overtime until almost 1 a.m. every day this week, and originally planned to go out for coffee today. But after turning off my alarm, I slept until noon, and even when my friend called me, I still didn’t get up. Looks like this sleep-debt goblin lost the weekend plans to the pillow again.

definition_tar_lang: Heading to an unfamiliar place with one quick glance at the route and no saved address, screenshots, or offline map. It usually starts with confidence and ends with repeated phone unlocking at random street corners.
sentence_in_context: 第一次去朋友新家还敢[MASK704]，结果在地铁口转了三圈。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I dared to go to my friend's new place with 'naked navigation' on my first visit, and ended up circling the subway exit three times.
paragraph_in_context: 出门前觉得自己方向感超强，瞄了一眼路线就收起手机。结果一路越走越心虚，路口停下来狂解锁。朋友问我到哪了，我只好承认今天在[MASK704]，马上就到是假的。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Before leaving, I felt like my sense of direction was amazing, so I just glanced at the route and put my phone away. But as I walked, I got less and less confident, stopping at intersections to frantically unlock my phone. When my friend asked where I was, I had to admit I was doing 'naked navigation' today, and that 'almost there' was a lie.

definition_tar_lang: Agreeing to a second caffeinated drink with no plan for sleep, stomach comfort, or the rest of your day. It captures that reckless moment of choosing immediate alertness over future consequences.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚只睡三小时，下午还敢[MASK705]，我是真拼了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I only slept three hours last night, and I still dared to go for a naked refill this afternoon—I’m really pushing it.
paragraph_in_context: 上午开会已经靠咖啡硬撑了。午饭后整个人发飘，同事一句走啊我就[MASK705]。现在心跳快得像开二倍速，今晚大概又别想早睡。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was already forcing myself through the morning meeting with coffee. After lunch I felt totally out of it, and when a coworker said “let’s go,” I went for a naked refill. Now my heart is racing like everything’s on 2x speed, and I probably shouldn’t expect an early night again.

definition_tar_lang: A friend who gets called in to witness and support a dramatic cleanup session, whether digital or emotional. They joke that their role is not to solve the problem, but to say 'yes, delete it' at the right moments.
sentence_in_context: 失恋后找了个[MASK706]，聊天记录终于清干净了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: After the breakup, I got a deletion buddy, and finally cleared out the chat history.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚又开始翻旧相册，越看越想发消息。幸好室友这个[MASK706]在线，边陪我骂边盯着我删。删完前任联系方式那一刻，整个人都轻了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night I started going through old photos again, and the more I looked, the more I wanted to send a message. Luckily my roommate, my deletion buddy, was online—cursing with me while watching me delete things. The moment I deleted my ex’s contact info, I felt so much lighter.

definition_tar_lang: Taking a nap with no alarm, no time check, and no agreement with reality about how long it will be. It usually means gambling the entire afternoon on the belief that 'just ten minutes' is still under your control.
sentence_in_context: 本来说[MASK707]十分钟，醒来天都快黑了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I said I'd take a “naked nap” for ten minutes, and when I woke up it was almost dark.
paragraph_in_context: 午饭后只想眯一下，结果开启了[MASK707]。眼睛一闭一睁，群消息99+，窗外都变色了。今天的计划表算是彻底作废。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: After lunch I only wanted to doze off for a bit, but it turned into a “naked nap.” I closed my eyes and opened them again, and the group chat had 99+ messages and the light outside had completely changed. Today’s schedule is basically ruined.

definition_tar_lang: Office workers who spend absurd amounts of time defending, optimizing, and emotionally attaching to their exact workstation. They know the best chair angle, outlet position, and monitor light better than they know the company strategy.
sentence_in_context: 别碰我显示器支架，[MASK708]真会急眼。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Don’t touch my monitor arm—an office workstation nerd will really lose it.
paragraph_in_context: 今天新来的同事随手换了我键盘和杯子的位置，我一上午都没进入状态。隔壁还笑我太夸张，说我这人就是标准[MASK708]。可等他坐我位子半小时，也开始调椅背和台灯了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Today the new coworker casually moved my keyboard and cup, and I couldn’t get into the zone all morning. The person next to me laughed and said I was such a classic workstation nerd. But after sitting at my desk for half an hour, he also started adjusting the chair back and desk lamp.

definition_tar_lang: People who specialize in slipping out of dinners, weddings, office events, or group outings without triggering a goodbye sequence. They see a clean exit as both a social skill and a survival mechanism.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚团建我又当了一回[MASK709]，谁都没发现。
sentence_in_context_gloss: At last night's team-building event, I pulled another stealth exit, and nobody noticed.
paragraph_in_context: 朋友婚礼真热闹，但我社交电量两小时就见底。敬完酒拍完照，我立刻切回[MASK709]模式。趁大家围着新人聊天，默默拿包溜走。到家那刻比抢到红包还开心。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: My friend's wedding was really lively, but my social battery was dead after just two hours. After the toast and photos, I immediately switched back into stealth-exit mode. While everyone was gathered around the newlyweds chatting, I quietly grabbed my bag and slipped away. Getting home made me happier than snagging a red envelope.

definition_tar_lang: Being abruptly inserted into a sign-up chain, payment list, attendance thread, or office task sequence with the expectation that you will continue it. The humor comes from how these chains make consent feel optional once your name appears.
sentence_in_context: 午休刚眯着就[MASK710]，奶茶名单又到我这了
sentence_in_context_gloss: I had just dozed off at lunch when I got pulled into the chain again—the milk tea order list landed on me.
paragraph_in_context: 本来只想安静下班，结果群里突然[MASK710]。前面已经排了十几个人，我名字都被顺手打上了。现在不回像装死，回了又得继续往下转。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I just wanted to get off work quietly, but suddenly I got dragged into a chain in the group chat. More than a dozen people were already listed before me, and someone had conveniently added my name too. Now if I don’t reply, it looks like I’m playing dead; if I do reply, I have to keep passing it on.

definition_tar_lang: People at parties, meetings, or weddings who instinctively migrate to edges, columns, walls, and corners where they can observe without becoming the center of interaction. They joke about being peripheral, but the position is chosen with strategy.
sentence_in_context: 同事婚礼我又当[MASK711]，靠墙端杯最自在。
sentence_in_context_gloss: At my coworker’s wedding I was a wallflower again, standing by the wall with a drink was the most comfortable.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚部门聚餐人超多，我一进门就自动贴边。朋友还没到前，我先在柱子旁观察全场。果然一整晚都很稳地做[MASK711]，等熟人来再慢慢加入聊天。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: There were so many people at the department dinner last night that I automatically drifted to the edge as soon as I walked in. Before my friends arrived, I stayed by a pillar and took in the whole room. Sure enough, I spent the whole night comfortably being a wallflower, only gradually joining the conversation once familiar people showed up.

definition_tar_lang: Joining a shared ride without checking the route order, pickup sequence, co-passengers, or whether the fare split actually makes sense. It names the gamble of getting into a logistical arrangement based purely on 'should be fine.'
sentence_in_context: 昨晚回家图省事[MASK712]，结果绕城一小时。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Last night I took a bare/shared ride just to save hassle getting home, and ended up circling the city for an hour.
paragraph_in_context: 下班太晚，地铁都快停了，我在群里随手约了个[MASK712]。上车才发现要先去接两个人，还得绕到反方向。司机说这样更顺路，我一路看导航一路后悔。以后宁愿多花点，也不想再赌这种运气。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I got off work too late and the subway was about to stop, so I casually arranged a bare/shared ride in a group chat. After getting in, I realized we had to pick up two other people first and even detour in the opposite direction. The driver said it was more efficient this way, and I spent the whole ride watching the map and regretting it. Next time I'd rather pay more than gamble on luck like this again.

definition_tar_lang: Visiting a friend or partner at work with no prior coordination, no clear timing, and no idea whether they are actually free. The awkwardness comes from arriving armed only with enthusiasm and discovering everyone else is still in full work mode.
sentence_in_context: 今天中午去公司[MASK713]，结果他在开会我像路人
sentence_in_context_gloss: At noon today I dropped by his office unannounced, and he was in a meeting, so I just felt like a random passerby.
paragraph_in_context: 本来想给她一个惊喜，下班前直接冲去她公司[MASK713]。前台让我先等等，我抱着奶茶站了二十分钟。她出来第一句竟然是：你怎么没提前说。浪漫值瞬间清零。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I wanted to surprise her, so I rushed to her office before she got off work and dropped by unannounced. The receptionist told me to wait, and I stood there holding milk tea for twenty minutes. The first thing she said when she came out was, 'Why didn't you tell me in advance?' The romance instantly dropped to zero.

definition_tar_lang: When someone quietly adds your item, preference, or name into a group order and informs you afterward as if it was helpful. It usually sounds efficient on paper, but leaves you stuck with a flavor, size, or payment split you never chose.
sentence_in_context: 奶茶群又把我[MASK714]了，到账单才知道
sentence_in_context_gloss: The milk tea group got me added in by default again—I only found out when the bill came.
paragraph_in_context: 中午大家点轻食，群里一阵接龙我没回。开会出来发现连酱料都替我选好了，备注写着“你应该也要”。这种[MASK714]真的很窒息，拒绝还像我扫兴。下次我直接关免打扰。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: At lunch everyone ordered salads, and the group chat was filling up while I didn’t reply. When I got out of the meeting, I found they had even chosen the sauce for me, with a note saying, “You probably want one too.” Being added in like this is really suffocating, and refusing makes me seem like the buzzkill. Next time I’m turning off notifications entirely.

definition_tar_lang: Someone obsessed with how much horizontal or visual breathing room objects have when laid out on a desk, tray, shelf, or photo. They keep nudging things apart or together until the spread feels balanced, even when nobody else noticed a problem.
sentence_in_context: 摆盘又被我重排三次，[MASK715]真的忍不住。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I rearranged the plating three times again—being a hand-width-spacing freak, I just can’t help it.
paragraph_in_context: 刚把书桌收好，杯子和台灯的位置又看着别扭。明明没差几厘米，我还是挪了半天。朋友进门只说挺整齐，我这个[MASK715]却终于顺眼了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I had just finished tidying my desk, but the cup and lamp placement still looked off. Even though it was only a few centimeters, I kept adjusting them for ages. My friend came in and just said it looked neat, but as a spacing freak, it finally looked right to me.

definition_tar_lang: This refers to people who constantly scan cafés, airports, libraries, and waiting areas for usable power outlets and move fast when one opens up. They often carry adapters, extension cords, or power banks and treat charging spots like scarce public resources.
sentence_in_context: 高铁站刚有人起身，旁边[MASK716]已经冲过去了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: At the high-speed rail station, someone had just stood up, and a power-outlet camper nearby already dashed over.
paragraph_in_context: 在机场候机三小时，手机和电脑都快没电了。刚看到角落有人拔线走开，几个[MASK716]立刻围上去。现在出门不带充电宝，真的一点安全感都没有。下次我也得学会提前踩点找插座。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was waiting at the airport for three hours, and both my phone and laptop were almost dead. As soon as I saw someone in the corner unplug and leave, several outlet hunters immediately crowded around. These days, going out without a power bank really gives me no sense of security. Next time I need to learn to scout out outlets in advance too.

definition_tar_lang: This means arriving at a new office, event venue, training session, or meetup with no idea where to go, what the process is, or what materials are needed. The person just shows up and hopes signs, staff, or other people will carry them through.
sentence_in_context: 第一次去培训我直接[MASK717]，连笔记本都没带。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The first time I went to the training, I showed up totally unprepared and didn’t even bring a notebook.
paragraph_in_context: 早上赶地铁差点迟到，到了新园区还找不到楼。因为昨晚没人通知流程，我今天基本是[MASK717]。前台让我先扫码登记，再去三楼领资料。幸好同组的人很热心，不然真要一直懵着。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was rushing for the subway this morning and almost arrived late, and when I got to the new campus I still couldn’t find the building. Since nobody told me the process last night, I basically showed up totally unprepared today. The front desk had me scan a code to register first, then go to the third floor to pick up materials. Luckily the people in my group were very helpful, otherwise I would have stayed completely confused.

definition_tar_lang: This is the person who always ends up summarizing what everyone meant, calming loose threads, and providing a final line that lets the group move on. They did not ask for this role, but somehow every messy discussion gets handed to them.
sentence_in_context: 这会开到最后，又是我当[MASK718]把话题拢住。
sentence_in_context_gloss: At the end of this meeting, it was me again playing the closer, pulling the discussion back together.
paragraph_in_context: 群里刚才又吵成一团，产品、运营、设计各说各的。眼看都要跑偏了，@我出来收一下。结果我这个[MASK718]又上线，发了三句总结，大家终于开始按那个版本做。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The group chat just turned into a mess again, with product, operations, and design all talking past each other. Just when it was about to go completely off track, they @'d me to step in. So my closer-dog mode kicked in again; I sent a three-line summary, and everyone finally started working from that version.

definition_tar_lang: This refers to people whose reflex at any small event is to raise their phone and document it before fully experiencing it. Whether it is cake arriving, a train passing, or someone unboxing something, their first response is always capture first, react later.
sentence_in_context: 和[MASK719]吃饭太真实，菜一上桌先别动
sentence_in_context_gloss: Eating with a phone-raising tribe is too real—the moment the dishes hit the table, nobody should touch them yet.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚去看烟花，旁边一排都是[MASK719]。刚炸开第一朵，大家先举手机找角度，欢呼都慢半拍。结果我回家翻相册，发现自己也拍了二十多段。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I went to watch fireworks last night, and a whole row beside me were phone-raising tribe types. As soon as the first burst went off, everyone lifted their phones to find the angle, and even the cheering came half a beat late. When I got home and checked my photos, I realized I’d recorded more than twenty clips too.

definition_tar_lang: This means the friend who gets asked to come along for small collection errands that technically do not require two people but somehow always become a paired activity. Their role is part company, part carrying help, part witness in case something goes wrong.
sentence_in_context: 又被叫去当[MASK720]，顺手还帮她拎了两袋快递。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Got called to be a 'pei qu gou' again, and ended up carrying two bags of packages for her too.
paragraph_in_context: 本来说只是下楼拿个件，结果她一个电话把我薅出去。到了站点才发现东西比想象中多，我这个[MASK720]直接上线。最后奶茶没白喝，至少还有人陪我一起累。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: She said it was just going downstairs to pick something up, but one call and she dragged me out. Once we got to the pickup point, we realized there was way more stuff than expected, so I instantly became the 'pei qu gou.' At least the milk tea wasn’t for nothing—someone suffered through it with me.

definition_tar_lang: Showing up to a social meetup without confirming the location, dress code, timing details, or even exactly who is coming. It captures the reckless confidence of heading out first and assuming the missing context will somehow sort itself out.
sentence_in_context: 朋友只说七点见，我又一次[MASK721]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: My friend only said “see you at seven,” and I showed up unprepared again.
paragraph_in_context: 群里临时喊吃饭，我没问地址就出门。到了地铁口才发现他们还没定哪家店，大家穿得也完全不是一个季节。每次这种[MASK721]，最后都靠定位共享救命。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The group suddenly called for dinner, and I left home without even asking for the address. When I got to the subway exit, I realized they still hadn’t decided which restaurant to go to, and everyone was dressed like they were in different seasons. Every time I do this kind of showing-up-unprepared, location sharing ends up saving my life.

definition_tar_lang: Adding your name to a group sign-up or response chain before reading what the event is, how much it costs, or whether you are even free that day. It is the behavior of trusting momentum more than information.
sentence_in_context: 群里一喊报名我就[MASK722]，结果那天还在出差。
sentence_in_context_gloss: As soon as the group called for sign-ups, I jumped in blindly, and it turned out I was still on a business trip that day.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚看到群里队形刷得飞快，我手一快也[MASK722]了。今天翻到前面才发现是周六早八爬山，还要自带早餐。现在只能一边后悔一边定闹钟。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night I saw the sign-up chain in the group moving really fast, and I impulsively added my name too. Today I scrolled up and realized it was for a Saturday 8 a.m. hiking trip, and we also have to bring our own breakfast. Now all I can do is regret it while setting my alarm.

definition_tar_lang: A self-aware label for people who quietly sample multiple chairs, corners, or positions before choosing where to stay. They are not being difficult; they just have a chronic need to find the least awkward, least exposed place to exist.
sentence_in_context: 每次进咖啡店我都先绕一圈，纯纯[MASK723]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Every time I enter a café, I walk around once first—I'm totally a chair-testing dog.
paragraph_in_context: 和朋友约饭，我又提前十分钟到店里。靠门太吵，里面那桌空调直吹，最后还是挪到角落。朋友一进门就笑：你这[MASK723]今天找到本命座了吗？
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I met friends for a meal and got to the restaurant ten minutes early again. The table by the door was too noisy, and the one inside was right under the AC, so I ended up moving to the corner. As soon as my friend walked in, they laughed: 'You chair-testing dog, did you find your soulmate seat today?'

definition_tar_lang: Being pulled into a group photo without checking your expression, posture, angle, or what your hands are doing. It refers to the vulnerable state of entering permanent visual evidence with zero readiness.
sentence_in_context: 每次聚餐最怕被喊过来[MASK724]，表情都来不及收拾。
sentence_in_context_gloss: At every group dinner, what I fear most is being suddenly called into a bare group photo—I don’t even have time to fix my expression.
paragraph_in_context: 刚拿起筷子准备开吃，旁边突然有人招手让我过去。人还没站稳就被拉着[MASK724]，刘海乱了脸也肿。照片一发群里，我直接失去今晚的社交勇气。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I had just picked up my chopsticks and was about to eat when someone next to me suddenly waved me over. Before I could even stand properly, I was dragged into a bare group photo; my bangs were a mess and my face looked swollen. Once the photo was posted in the group chat, I instantly lost all social courage for the night.

definition_tar_lang: Someone who gets disproportionate satisfaction from leaving one extra slot free in a bag, drawer, app layout, or schedule. They dislike systems filled to 100 percent and become emotionally attached to the safety of a little unused space.
sentence_in_context: 行李箱还空一格我就安心，纯纯[MASK725]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: As long as there's still one slot left in the suitcase, I feel at ease — total yucaokong.
paragraph_in_context: 整理桌面时我死活不肯把最后一格放满。图标挤太紧我会莫名烦躁，宁可翻第二页。朋友笑我这是[MASK725]，我居然觉得被说中了。现在连日程表都要留点白。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: When organizing my desktop, I absolutely refuse to fill the very last slot. If the icons are packed too tightly, I get inexplicably irritated and would rather swipe to a second page. My friend joked that I'm a yucaokong, and honestly it felt accurate. Now I even need to leave a little blank space in my schedule.

definition_tar_lang: This means the friend who gets invited out not because they love the event, but because they are expected to document it from ten flattering angles. They usually carry bags, watch belongings, and hear 'one more shot' far more than they get to enjoy the outing themselves.
sentence_in_context: 出来玩一下午，我又成了全程[MASK726]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: We went out all afternoon, and I ended up being the full-time photo sidekick again.
paragraph_in_context: 本来说好一起逛市集，结果她一路试妆换角度。我手里拎着奶茶和外套，还得帮她找光。最后相册里全是她的美照，我这个[MASK726]连张单人照都没有。

definition_tar_lang: A vibe centered on mild delay, soft expressions, and a gentle not-quite-caught-up energy. It feels cute not because it is polished, but because it seems one beat behind the world in an endearing way.

sentence_in_context_gloss: Going to the suburbs with friends to see an exhibition, and I’m doing a bare-route lookup again.

When I got to the office today, the whole floor looked like it had been pushed into the same item. We say we chose it ourselves, but really the choice was gone long ago.

definition_tar_lang: Picking a side instantly in a debate or group conflict without knowing the backstory, evidence, or stakes. It usually ends with the realization that your confident position was built on vibes alone.

definition_tar_lang: Joining a meeting with no context, no document, and no idea whether you were actually supposed to speak. The term captures that exposed feeling of trying to infer the agenda in real time.

definition_tar_lang: When someone casually includes you in a class, event, volunteer shift, or group plan without really asking first. It often comes wrapped in the assumption that 'you were coming anyway,' which is exactly why it feels annoying.

sentence_in_context_gloss: As soon as the roster was posted in the group chat, I realized I'd been signed up along with everyone else again.

Now if I don't go, I look like I'm not being a team player.

definition_tar_lang: People who arrange their day with almost theatrical precision around countdowns, transit arrival minutes, check-out times, and delivery windows. They are not generally organized in life; they are specifically organized around timing friction.

sentence_in_context_gloss: To line up my delivery and the subway just right, I’ve evolved into a timing-clinger.

My friend laughed that I’m usually forgetful, yet at times like this I seem superpowered. Can’t help it—the joy of a timing-clinger is when everything lands just right.

definition_tar_lang: Someone fascinated by the feeling of moving from one setting to another rather than the destination itself. They care about corridor lighting, elevator music, station exits, and the emotional texture of in-between moments.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: After landing on a business trip, I didn’t rush to get a taxi and instead took a slow walk through the connecting corridor. The handoff between the hotel elevator music, the mall’s air conditioning, and the evening breeze at the street corner was especially intoxicating. definition_tar_lang: [MASK760] means showing up to a social event with basically no situational knowledge: you do not know who is coming, what the dress code is, or what the social dynamics will be. It captures that exposed feeling of entering a fully formed group setup with zero intel.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: A friend dragged me to a gathering last minute, saying everyone was easy to get along with, so I agreed. When I got there, I realized they were all her grad school classmates and I didn’t know a single one. I was also dressed wrong and couldn’t get into the flow of conversation at all. Most awkward blind-arrival social situation of the year—I spent the trip home replaying everything.

definition_tar_lang: A [MASK761] cannot leave charging cables, headphone cords, or desk wires in a messy tangle. They automatically straighten, align, loop, and separate them, often feeling disproportionate relief once everything runs in clean lines.
sentence_in_context: 出门前又把耳机线捋直了，我这[MASK761]没救
sentence_in_context_gloss: Before heading out I straightened my earphone cable again—I'm hopelessly a cable-line neat freak.
paragraph_in_context: 同事借我充电器，用完随手一塞就还我。 我接过来第一反应不是收包，是先把线重新绕好。 可能我真是[MASK761]，看到桌上七扭八歪的线就浑身难受。 理顺之后，心情都跟着平了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: A coworker borrowed my charger and just stuffed it back before returning it. My first reaction when I took it wasn't to put it in my bag, but to rewind the cable neatly. I might really be a cable-line neat freak—seeing wires twisted all over the desk makes me feel physically uncomfortable. Once I straightened them out, my mood settled too.

definition_tar_lang: This is the person who keeps experimenting with clothing combinations, accessories, or room setups that looked better in theory than in reality. The label is self-aware and affectionate, implying repeated hopeful attempts followed by immediate visual regret.
sentence_in_context: 新买的披肩和耳环一上身，我又成[MASK762]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The moment I put on the new shawl and earrings, I became a "trial-styling dog" again.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I originally wanted to move the little tea table by the window and pair it with that floor lamp. It looked atmospheric in photos, but once arranged at home it just blocked the way. After half an hour of tinkering, I sat on the floor and sighed: the "trial-styling dog" lost again today. I’ll probably still keep trying tomorrow.

definition_tar_lang: [MASK763] refers to an aesthetic where nearly empty coffee cups, softened ice, lipstick marks, and the after-feel of a finished drink become part of the mood. It conveys a lived-in, post-conversation visual atmosphere rather than a fresh, polished one.
sentence_in_context: 这组咖啡店随拍太[MASK763]了，越看越有故事感。
sentence_in_context_gloss: These casual coffee shop shots are so [MASK763]; the more I look, the more they feel full of stories.
paragraph_in_context: 本来只想拍今天的拿铁，结果最后几张最好看。冰块化了一半，杯沿还蹭到一点口红。朋友走后桌面安静下来，突然很有[MASK763]的感觉，像聊天刚散场。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I originally just wanted to photograph today's latte, but the last few shots turned out best. The ice had melted halfway, and there was even a little lipstick on the rim. After my friend left, the table went quiet, and it suddenly felt very [MASK763], like a conversation had just ended.

definition_tar_lang: [MASK764] means impulsively moving to a new table or seat without checking basics like outlets, lighting, noise level, or whether someone else is about to take it. It captures that reckless little relocation decision made entirely on a momentary feeling.
sentence_in_context: 图一时清净[MASK764]，结果新位子没插座。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I impulsively switched tables for a bit of peace and quiet, and the new seat didn’t even have an outlet.
paragraph_in_context: 下午在咖啡店改稿，嫌旁边聊天太吵，我一冲动就[MASK764]。刚坐下才发现这边灯暗、空调直吹，手机也快没电。果然别只凭感觉挪位置。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was revising drafts at a café in the afternoon, and the people next to me were chatting too loudly, so I impulsively switched tables. As soon as I sat down, I realized the lighting was dim, the AC was blowing right on me, and my phone was almost out of battery. Sure enough, you shouldn’t move seats based on vibes alone.

definition_tar_lang: [MASK765] are people who repeatedly gather around shared cabinets, office supply cupboards, or storage lockers at the exact times everyone else needs them too. It describes a tiny but real congestion culture around communal storage points.
sentence_in_context: 每次开会前茶水间都被[MASK765]堵死，拿个杯子像闯关。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Before every meeting, the pantry gets completely blocked by the cabinet-hogging crowd; grabbing a cup feels like clearing a game level.
paragraph_in_context: 我们楼层的打印区最近又开始排队。明明只想拿一包纸，结果储物柜前站满人。最神奇的是他们总挑最忙的时候出现，活脱脱一群[MASK765]。现在我都学会错峰去拿东西了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The printing area on our floor has started getting crowded again lately. I just wanted to grab a pack of paper, but the storage cabinet was surrounded by people. The weirdest part is that they always show up at the busiest times—a perfect example of the cabinet-guarding crowd. Now I’ve learned to go fetch things at off-peak times.

definition_tar_lang: [MASK766] means handing over your bag or items for temporary storage without sorting valuables, checking claim details, or planning what you might suddenly need later. It names that careless trust move people make when they're already overloaded or rushing.
sentence_in_context: 赶高铁时又[MASK766]，充电宝和证件差点拿不回
sentence_in_context_gloss: While rushing to catch the high-speed rail, I did a naked bag drop again, and almost couldn’t get my power bank and ID back.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: The locker line at the mall was super long, so to save time I just handed my backpack to the front desk. Right when the movie started, I remembered my earbuds were still inside. My friend laughed that I always do this kind of naked bag drop whenever I go out; when I’m in a rush, I’ll shove anything in there. Next time I should take out the stuff I’ll need first.

definition_tar_lang: Someone who jokes that they are always the one used as the safe example, the less photogenic option, or the trial run before the real choice. The term carries mild resignation and group familiarity rather than serious bitterness.
sentence_in_context: 合照一发出来，我这[MASK767]又成功衬托全员了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: As soon as the group photo was posted, I, the fallback dog, once again successfully made everyone else look better.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: My friend bought lipstick and had me try the shade first, saying once she saw it on me she'd know whether to go for it. In the end she turned around and ordered the popular color, while I was responsible for providing warning data. Oh well, being the fallback dog still means maximum participation—I didn’t go out for nothing at least.

definition_tar_lang: Taking a queue number at a clinic, restaurant, or service center without checking how long the line is, whether you brought the right documents, or what you'll do while waiting. It captures a very recognizable form of reckless optimism.

It turned out I hadn’t prepared anything, and my phone battery was only at 8%. On a whim I just blindly took a queue number, and now I’m sitting in the hallway questioning my life. There are still more than twenty people ahead of me, and my afternoon meeting is about to start.

definition_tar_lang: People who visit a market, café, park, or pop-up mainly to absorb the atmosphere for a short, perfect window. They are there for the exact texture of the moment, not for staying long or consuming much.

After taking two photos, I left without even ordering a second drink. My friend laughed that I was indulging my "vibe-catcher" habit again, but this kind of brief stay is really addictive.

My reverse-order compulsion kicked in, so I went to read the earliest leaks and original post first. By the time I caught up to today, the narrative had already changed again. Now I’m afraid anything I say will be based on an outdated version.

sentence_in_context_gloss: I only realized at the health exam today that I’d gone in completely unprepared—wasted a trip.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: My alarm went off late, but I still rushed to the health check center. Only when I got there did I learn I needed to be fasting, and I hadn’t even saved a screenshot of my booking code. The front desk saw my confused face and said this basically counted as a bare-booking health exam. Now I’m riding the subway back to the office, and the more I think about it, the more embarrassing it feels.

On the way downstairs I realized I'd forgotten both my water bottle and charger—today is basically a bare commute. Even worse, I still have a meeting this afternoon, so all I can do is pray nothing else goes wrong.

definition_tar_lang: A visual style that looks pristine, glossy, and almost unopened, as if every object and outfit is still in protective wrap. It gives off a carefully preserved, untouched, showroom-like feeling.

sentence_in_context_gloss: Her outfit today is so plastic-wrap style, like she just walked out of a display window.
paragraph_in_context: 周末去看展，前排那个女生真的很抓眼。白衬衫一点褶都没有，球鞋也亮得离谱。整个人是那种[MASK773]氛围，干净到像自带打光。随手一拍都像品牌图。

Her white shirt didn’t have a single wrinkle, and her sneakers were absurdly shiny. Her whole vibe was that plastic-wrap style, so clean it looked like she had her own lighting. Any random photo looked like a brand campaign.

definition_tar_lang: This means going into a presentation, speech, recording, or group performance without rehearsing once beforehand. It often carries a mix of reckless confidence and quiet panic, especially when the person is counting on improvisation to replace preparation.
sentence_in_context: 明天路演我居然还在[MASK774]，心跳已经超速了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: My pitch is tomorrow and I’m somehow still going in unrehearsed; my heart is already racing.
paragraph_in_context: PPT刚改完，主持词也还是零碎的。朋友问我今晚要不要顺一遍，我嘴硬说临场发挥更真。结果现在越想越慌，感觉这次又是在[MASK774]。希望上台别卡壳。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I just finished revising the PPT, and my script is still all over the place. A friend asked if I wanted to run through it tonight, and I stubbornly said improvising would feel more authentic. But now the more I think about it, the more nervous I get—it feels like I’m going in unrehearsed again. Hope I don’t freeze on stage.

definition_tar_lang: An aesthetic built around temporary-stay energy: folded clothes not fully unpacked, chargers visible, one useful cup, and a room that never feels fully settled. It suggests a life always half-ready to leave, even when the person has lived there for months.
sentence_in_context: 租了半年还像[MASK775]，箱子一直没收完。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I've rented this place for half a year and it still feels "guest-stay style"; I never finished unpacking my boxes.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Friends who visit my place all say it looks like a model Airbnb room. There's always a charging cable by the bed, only one cup on the desk, and my clothes are still folded instead of put away. definition_tar_lang: Quickly skimming posts, summaries, or hot takes so you can sound informed in conversation without understanding the subject deeply. It names the shell-level literacy built by feed culture.

definition_tar_lang: The pattern of tapping likes on someone's posts to maintain a bond, signal support, or hint at continued presence instead of actually messaging them. It names a low-risk dependency on tiny visible gestures.
sentence_in_context: 他又来我朋友圈[MASK864]了，偏偏就是不回消息。
sentence_in_context_gloss: He came to my Moments to do that 'zanlai' thing again, yet still won't reply to my messages.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: We haven't had a real conversation in half a month. But every day he likes the new photos I post, and sometimes even goes back to like much older updates. My friend says this is 'zanlai.' It looks like he hasn't gone far, but he hasn't come any closer either.

definition_tar_lang: When you cannot begin because you are too attached to the perfect future version of the project, trip, post, or life change. The fantasy does not motivate action; it jams it.

But the more I thought about it, the more I felt the first video had to be amazing. Tonight I only ended up organizing materials again and still didn’t press record—classic dream-stuck.

definition_tar_lang: The reflex to bring snacks, over-thank people, send little gifts, or be extra courteous because you are too nervous to take up space normally. It is anxiety translated into generosity.

definition_tar_lang: The habit of bookmarking posts, videos, or links with the solemn idea that you'll return when you have the 'right mood' to judge whether they're actually good. In practice, the saved pile becomes a museum of postponed discernment.

Every time I just got into the zone, I wanted to tap open messages, and my mind got pulled away. A friend asked me to go out, and I said, “Wait a bit”—I’m really too good at this whole stockpiling-leisure thing.

definition_tar_lang: The mental freeze that happens right before paying for something you technically can afford but emotionally cannot process as worth the price. It is a momentary paralysis caused by price-to-desire conflict.

sentence_in_context_gloss: Tonight I watched other people's decluttering videos again—so "daisong."

I'll deal with it tomorrow.

definition_tar_lang: The illusion of closeness produced by repeatedly photographing, tagging, or appearing in content with someone, even though your real relationship remains shallow. Camera proximity starts impersonating social intimacy.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Lately, at every event he’s been pulling me into the same frame, and on social media it looks like we’re together every day. But today we ran into each other on the street, and he froze for two seconds before remembering my name. So being photo-familiar is one thing; in private it’s still a bit awkward.

definition_tar_lang: The frantic act of googling medical tips, gift lists, or elder-care advice right after a parent mentions a problem, as a way to feel useful before doing anything concrete. Concern becomes a search behavior.
sentence_in_context: 我妈一说膝盖疼，我又开始半夜[MASK876]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The moment my mom said her knee hurt, I started 'search-filiality' again in the middle of the night.
paragraph_in_context: 爸昨晚随口说了句睡不好，我立刻收藏了十几篇助眠攻略。药枕、泡脚桶、褪黑素看了一圈，购物车先满上。结果今天还没来得及陪他去医院，只顾着在那儿[MASK876]。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night my dad casually mentioned he wasn't sleeping well, and I immediately saved more than a dozen sleep-improvement guides. I looked through herbal pillows, foot-soaking tubs, and melatonin, and filled up my cart first. But today I still haven't had time to go with him to the hospital—I've just been stuck there doing 'search-filiality.'

definition_tar_lang: The mental maneuver of enduring an overpriced purchase by repeatedly reframing it as an investment in health, taste, efficiency, or adulthood. You’re not just paying too much—you’re emotionally amortizing it.

sentence_in_context_gloss: This coffee is ridiculously expensive, but for surviving an 8 a.m. start, I can only just swallow the cost.
paragraph_in_context: 昨天咬牙买了那台贵价吹风机，付款时手都在抖。回家吹完头发居然真的快很多，头皮也没那么难受。我一边心疼余额一边安慰自己，这波算[MASK877]吧。成年人的安全感，有时真是花钱买来的。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday I grit my teeth and bought that overpriced hair dryer, and my hands were shaking when I paid. After using it at home, drying my hair really was much faster, and my scalp felt less irritated. While feeling bad for my bank balance, I kept telling myself this counts as "ren gui." Sometimes an adult’s sense of security really is something you buy with money.

definition_tar_lang: Reopening old chats, saved voice notes, or buried posts to squeeze one more dose of emotional sweetness out of a relationship or crush that is already fading. It’s affection retrieved from the archive.

sentence_in_context_gloss: At dawn I went digging for sweetness again; after listening to that voice note, I actually smiled.
paragraph_in_context: 本来都准备把聊天记录清空了，结果手一滑点开去年的置顶。看到那句晚安又开始[MASK878]，连他发错的表情包都顺眼了。人果然一想念就没出息。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was ready to clear out our chat history, but then my hand slipped and opened last year's pinned messages. Seeing that 'good night' made me start digging for sweetness again—even the meme he sent by mistake looked cute. Missing someone really makes you pathetic.

definition_tar_lang: The state where you keep mechanically replying to messages, comments, or work chats until your words feel emotionally dead and interchangeable.
sentence_in_context: 今天从早回消息到现在，整个人都[MASK879]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I’ve been replying to messages nonstop since morning, and now I’m completely reply-numb.

definition_tar_lang: Staying awake longer than planned because a post is still getting engagement and you don't want to miss the live drip of reactions.
sentence_in_context: 本来说刷完就睡，结果评论区太热闹，直接[MASK880]到两点。

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Tonight I was supposed to put my phone away at eleven. Then that rant post suddenly started getting shared, and the comments kept coming one after another. Every time I tried to sleep, I wanted to check just one more time, so I kept staying up for the engagement. By morning, I was so sleepy in the meeting that my soul had left my body.

definition_tar_lang: The habit of screenshotting kind messages, compliments, or tiny moments of care as emotional backup for future bad days.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚又去翻[MASK881]，看到那句晚安还是鼻酸。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Last night I went back through my warmth-screenshots again; seeing that goodnight message still made my nose sting.
paragraph_in_context: 今天被工作怼到没脾气，回家路上整个人都空了。洗完澡躺床上，顺手翻了翻[MASK881]。那些零碎的偏爱和惦记，居然比热水还管用。明天再撑一下吧。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Work beat me down today, and on the way home I felt completely drained. After showering and lying in bed, I casually looked through my warmth-screenshots. Those little fragments of affection and care were somehow even more effective than hot water. I’ll hang in there again tomorrow.

definition_tar_lang: Watching a post, project, or release so obsessively that you experience its poor performance in real time, almost as a ritual of self-torment.
sentence_in_context: 新剧一上线我就开始[MASK882]，越看数据越心梗。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The moment the new drama went live, I started doom-watching it flop; the more I watched the numbers, the more my chest hurt.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I told myself I wouldn't check the first-day stats, but I still got up in the middle of the night to refresh. It never made the trending list, and the views showed no sign of picking up; the group chat went totally silent. I'm hopeless but can't help myself—I latched onto this project and obsessively watched it flop until dawn.

definition_tar_lang: The private fantasy loop where you imagine a completely ordinary post suddenly exploding and rewriting your whole social status.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚又犯[MASK883]了，发张猫图都想冲上热搜。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I had another bout of menghong last night—even posting a cat photo, I imagined it shooting up to trending.
paragraph_in_context: 本来只想随手记录下下班晚霞，修图都没认真修。结果发出去三分钟，我已经开始[MASK883]，连采访怎么说都脑补好了。朋友看完只回我一句：先别飘，点赞才7个。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I originally just wanted to casually record the sunset after work and didn’t even edit the photo carefully. But three minutes after posting it, I was already in menghong mode, even scripting in my head what I’d say in an interview. After seeing it, my friend replied with just one line: don’t get carried away yet, it only has 7 likes.

definition_tar_lang: The sudden emotional recoil after a moment of unexpected closeness, when you start pulling back, deleting, or toning down messages to restore distance.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚聊太上头，今早突然[MASK884]，把语音都删了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: We got way too into chatting last night; this morning I suddenly pulled back and even deleted the voice messages.
paragraph_in_context: 本来只是随手回他一句，结果越聊越晚。凌晨那会儿还觉得好像靠近了一点。早上醒来就开始[MASK884]，朋友圈也设置成仅三天可见。人果然最会自己给自己降温。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: It started with just a casual reply to him, but we ended up chatting later and later. Around midnight, it even felt like we had gotten a little closer. When I woke up in the morning, I started pulling back, and even changed my Moments to visible for only three days. People really are the best at cooling themselves down.

definition_tar_lang: The subtle social-media flex where someone frames test prep, certifications, or intellectual suffering as humble self-reporting, but the real point is displaying superiority. It names bragging through disciplined misery.
sentence_in_context: 又发凌晨四点刷题照，这波[MASK885]太熟练了吧。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Posting another 4 a.m. study photo—this exam-flexing is getting way too polished.
paragraph_in_context: 朋友说只是记录备考日常，结果九宫格全是模考分数和咖啡杯。每次配文都写快崩溃了，好像谁没熬过夜一样。看久了只觉得这不是分享，是标准[MASK885]。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: My friend says they're just documenting daily exam prep, but the whole nine-photo post is mock exam scores and coffee cups. Every caption says they're on the verge of collapse, like no one else has ever stayed up late. After seeing it enough, it stops feeling like sharing and starts looking like classic exam-flexing.

definition_tar_lang: Turning your own self-awareness into a brand—publicly analyzing your flaws, motives, and delusions in a way that is also meant to impress. It is insight performed as charisma.
sentence_in_context: 他直播里边自嘲边剖析自己，简直是高级[MASK886]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: In his livestream, he mocked himself while dissecting his own behavior—basically high-level xingxiu.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚看他采访，越看越觉得会说。明明在讲自己拧巴和虚荣，却句句都像在立人设。那种半真半演的[MASK886]，居然还挺有感染力。评论区一边骂装，一边疯狂转发。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I watched his interview last night, and the more I watched, the more I felt he really knew how to talk. He was clearly talking about his own inner conflict and vanity, yet every line felt like branding himself. That half-real, half-performed xingxiu was strangely compelling. The comments were split between calling him fake and reposting like crazy.

definition_tar_lang: The laziness triggered by seeing extremely optimized routines, products, or lifestyles that make your own effort feel not worth starting. Instead of motivating you, 'perfect fit' content drains your will to act.
sentence_in_context: 刷到别人七分钟备餐教程，我直接[MASK887]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I saw someone else's seven-minute meal-prep tutorial and instantly felt [MASK887].
paragraph_in_context: 本来想收拾房间，结果刷到一堆极简收纳博主。人家连抽屉分区都像样板间，我看完只想躺回床上。不是不想动，是越看越[MASK887]，连垃圾都懒得先扔。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was going to tidy my room, but then I scrolled past a bunch of minimalist organization bloggers. Even their drawer dividers looked like showroom displays, and after watching I just wanted to lie back down on the bed. It's not that I don't want to do anything—it's that the more I watch, the more [MASK887] I feel, to the point that I can't even be bothered to throw out the trash first.

definition_tar_lang: To repeatedly reopen a chat thread or profile before sleeping, hoping for a new message even though you know none is coming. It describes that restless, half-automatic checking behavior at night.
sentence_in_context: 又[MASK888]到两点，手机亮了十几次都不是你。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I ended up doom-checking before sleep until 2 a.m.; my phone lit up more than a dozen times and none of them were from you.
paragraph_in_context: 说好早点睡，结果还是在[MASK888]。明知道他今晚不会回，手却总想点开那个对话框。窗外都安静了，只有消息页被我来回刷亮。算了，明天起床再笑自己没出息。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I said I’d sleep early, but I still ended up rechecking before bed. I know he won’t reply tonight, but my hand keeps wanting to open that chat window. Outside it’s already quiet, and only the message page keeps lighting up from me refreshing it again and again. Whatever—tomorrow I’ll laugh at myself for being so hopeless.

definition_tar_lang: To leave a message unread on purpose for a while so your reply feels less eager. It refers to a mild, calculated delay rather than full-on ignoring someone.
sentence_in_context: 他秒回我三次，我决定先[MASK889]十分钟。
sentence_in_context_gloss: He replied to me instantly three times, so I decided to leave him on read for ten minutes first.
paragraph_in_context: 姐妹说我太好懂，消息一来就回。今晚他又问我要不要见面，我看了半天没动。不是不想理，就是想先[MASK889]一下，免得显得我太上头。结果他居然主动打电话来了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: My friend said I’m too easy to read—I reply as soon as a message comes in. Tonight he asked again if I wanted to meet up, and I stared at it for a long while without doing anything. It’s not that I don’t want to respond; I just want to leave him on read for a bit so I don’t seem too invested. And then he actually took the initiative to call me.

definition_tar_lang: To abruptly shut down a discussion because continuing it would expose too much emotion, conflict, or weakness. It suggests ending the whole setup instead of arguing point by point.
sentence_in_context: 他一被追问就[MASK890]退群，谁还敢认真聊。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The moment he got pressed with questions, he flipped the table and left the group—who would still dare to talk seriously?
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚群里本来还在对方案。说到预算和责任划分，有人语气一下就冲了。结果他没接话，直接[MASK890]下线。留我们几个看着聊天记录发愣。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night the group was still discussing the proposal. When it got to budget and division of responsibility, someone’s tone suddenly got sharp. He didn’t respond at all and just flipped the table and went offline. The rest of us were left staring at the chat log in a daze.

definition_tar_lang: To suddenly change the emotional rules of a relationship without discussing it, such as becoming colder, more formal, or less accessible. The bond still exists, but the way in has changed.
sentence_in_context: 昨天还秒回，今天突然[MASK891]，我有点懵。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Yesterday they replied instantly, but today they suddenly changed the vibe; I'm a bit confused.
paragraph_in_context: 前阵子我们还什么都聊，半夜也会互发语音。结果这周他像[MASK891]了一样，回复变得很客气，见面也总说忙。关系好像没断，可就是回不到以前那种自然。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: A while ago we talked about everything and even sent voice messages late at night. But this week it's like he suddenly changed the rules of the relationship: his replies became very polite, and whenever we meet he always says he's busy. The relationship doesn't seem broken, but it just can't go back to how natural it used to feel.

definition_tar_lang: To disappear into domestic chores, errands, or practical tasks when you do not want to think about a larger emotional problem. It describes avoidance through ordinary busyness.
sentence_in_context: 这周又开始[MASK892]，把家里角角落落都收拾了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I started chenpen again this week, cleaning every corner of the house.
paragraph_in_context: 本来想认真聊聊那件事，结果一回家就开始[MASK892]。洗衣服、拖地、买菜排满了晚上。忙到停下来那一刻，还是得面对没说出口的话。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I had meant to seriously talk about that issue, but as soon as I got home I slipped into chenpen. Laundry, mopping, and grocery shopping filled the whole evening. The moment I finally stopped, I still had to face the words left unsaid.

definition_tar_lang: To spend an absurd amount of time refining tiny wording choices in a message, caption, or email. It implies careful picking through details that probably do not matter as much as they feel like they do.
sentence_in_context: 这条朋友圈我又[MASK893]半小时，还是发了删。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I spent another half hour fussing over this Moments post, and still posted and deleted it.
paragraph_in_context: 本来想秒回老板邮件，结果开头一句改了十遍。越看越觉得语气不对，又把结尾挪来挪去。我真是太会[MASK893]了，折腾到午休都没发出去。最后同事看了一眼，说就这样吧。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I originally wanted to reply to my boss’s email right away, but I rewrote the opening line ten times. The more I looked at it, the more the tone felt off, so I kept moving the ending around too. I’m seriously too prone to obsessing over wording, and by lunch break I still hadn’t sent it. In the end, a coworker glanced at it and said, ‘Just send it like this.’

definition_tar_lang: To emotionally prepare yourself for leaving a job, city, relationship, or group before you have actually made the move. It is the stage where part of you is already gone.
sentence_in_context: 会还没开完，我心里已经开始[MASK894]了。
sentence_in_context_gloss: The meeting isn’t even over yet, but in my heart I’ve already started packing to leave.
paragraph_in_context: 这周还是照常打卡、改方案、回消息。可每次走出办公室，我都觉得自己在[MASK894]。不是突然想辞职，只是那股留下来的劲慢慢没了。可能人真正离开前，心会先一步出发。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: This week I’m still clocking in, revising plans, and replying to messages like usual. But every time I walk out of the office, I feel like I’m already emotionally packing to leave. It’s not that I suddenly want to quit; it’s just that my drive to stay is slowly fading. Maybe before a person really leaves, the heart sets out first.

definition_tar_lang: To give an opinion with full confidence despite having only surface-level knowledge from headlines, clips, or reposts. The outside shape is there, but there is nothing substantial inside.
sentence_in_context: 别光刷了几个短视频就来[MASK895]，真相没你想的简单。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Don’t watch a few short videos and then start bluffing with confidence; the truth isn’t as simple as you think.
paragraph_in_context: 群里刚聊到新政策，他看了个营销号总结就开始[MASK895]。别人贴了原文，他又装没看见。最离谱的是语气还特别笃定，像自己参与制定的一样。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The group had just started discussing the new policy, and after reading a summary from a clickbait account, he started confidently bluffing. When others posted the original text, he pretended not to see it. The wildest part was how certain he sounded, like he had helped draft it himself.

definition_tar_lang: To build up a convincing public image of productivity by arranging many small visible signs—notes, tabs, coffee photos, calendar screenshots—whether or not much real work is being done. It is the aesthetic construction of diligence.
sentence_in_context: 今天没推进多少，但工位[MASK896]贴得像冲刺周。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I didn't make much progress today, but my desk looked as if it were sprint week from all the 'tiling'.
paragraph_in_context: 早上先拍了咖啡和待办，群里顺手发了日程截图。开了两小时会，真正动手也没几分钟。结果同事路过还夸我最近好自律，看来[MASK896]确实有点用。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: In the morning I first took photos of my coffee and to-do list, then casually posted a screenshot of my schedule in the group chat. After two hours of meetings, I barely had a few minutes to actually do any work. A colleague passed by and even praised me for being so disciplined lately—looks like 'tiling' really does work a little.

definition_tar_lang: To intentionally delay replying after a social event, date, or interview so you do not seem too eager. It describes the cooling-off pause people perform for image management rather than for any real practical reason.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚聊得超投缘，我还是先[MASK897]两天再回她。
sentence_in_context_gloss: We really hit it off last night, but I’m still going to leave it on ice for two days before replying to her.
paragraph_in_context: 面完试其实感觉不错，HR今天就来问到岗时间。朋友叫我别秒回，先[MASK897]一下显得稳重。可我怕拖太久，对方以为我没兴趣。你们通常会等多久？
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The interview actually felt pretty good, and HR already asked today when I could start. My friend told me not to reply instantly and to leave it on ice a bit so I seem more composed. But I’m worried that if I wait too long, they’ll think I’m not interested. How long do you all usually wait?

definition_tar_lang: To present different versions of your personality to different social circles and keep them carefully separated. It is especially used when friends from work, family, fandom, and dating life must not compare notes.
sentence_in_context: 我平时超会[MASK898]，团建和漫展像两个人。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I'm usually great at keeping my worlds separate; at team-building and at conventions I seem like two different people.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚差点社死。下班和同事吃饭，结果隔壁桌坐着我追星搭子。她刚想大声叫我ID，我疯狂使眼色让她别说。[MASK898]分了三年，差点一夜翻车。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I almost died of embarrassment last night. I was having dinner with coworkers after work, and at the next table was my fandom buddy. She was just about to loudly call me by my online handle, and I frantically signaled for her not to. I've kept these sides of my life separate for three years, and it almost all crashed in one night.

definition_tar_lang: To leave small pessimistic remarks in advance so that if things go badly, you can claim you already expected it. It is a form of low-key emotional risk control common before exams, launches, confessions, or performances.
sentence_in_context: 明天答辩先[MASK899]，免得到时候翻车太难受。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I’m laying some salt before tomorrow’s defense, so it won’t hurt as much if it goes badly.
paragraph_in_context: 新品今晚开售，群里大家都在倒计时。我先[MASK899]一下，别到时候库存秒空我又抢不到。话先放这，能买到当然最好。买不到我就当省钱了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The new product goes on sale tonight, and everyone in the group chat is counting down. I’m going to lay some salt first, in case it sells out instantly and I can’t get one again. I’m saying this now—of course it’d be best if I can buy it. If not, I’ll just treat it as saving money.

definition_tar_lang: To quietly clean up your own involvement in a messy online situation by deleting traces, unliking posts, or editing wording before anyone checks receipts. It suggests removing just enough evidence to look uninvolved.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚还在带节奏，今早就开始[MASK900]了？
sentence_in_context_gloss: You were stirring things up last night, and now this morning you’re already covering your tracks?
paragraph_in_context: 热搜一挂出来，群里突然安静了。刚才还转发得起劲的人，一个个把赞撤了，文案也改得很干净。别装路人了，这波明显是在[MASK900]。可惜截图早就有人存好了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: As soon as the topic hit trending, the group suddenly went quiet. The people who were enthusiastically reposting earlier started removing likes one by one, and even cleaned up their captions. Stop pretending to be bystanders—this is obviously people covering their tracks. Too bad someone already saved the screenshots.

definition_tar_lang: To hide a personal motive inside an apparently practical invitation or plan. For example, asking someone to join an event mainly because you want one-on-one time, but framing it as convenience or spare seats.
sentence_in_context: 他说顺路送我回家，结果一路都在[MASK901]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: He said he was just giving me a ride home on the way, but the whole ride he was clearly slipping in his real agenda.
paragraph_in_context: 本来以为他拉群约爬山，是刚好多一张票。结果临出发前又单独来问我能不能早点到，我才反应过来他在[MASK901]。朋友还笑我，说这么明显你现在才懂。下次我可不装傻了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: At first I thought he started the group chat for the hike because he happened to have one extra ticket. But right before we left, he messaged me separately asking if I could arrive early, and only then did I realize he was slipping in his real motive. My friend even laughed at me, saying it was so obvious and I only just got it. Next time I’m not going to play dumb.

definition_tar_lang: To quietly coordinate your wording, memory, or public timeline with someone else so your accounts match. Common in office situations, relationship cover stories, or friend-group damage control.
sentence_in_context: 先别回群里消息，我跟你[MASK902]一下再说。
sentence_in_context_gloss: Don’t reply in the group chat yet; let me sync stories with you first.
paragraph_in_context: 领导突然问昨晚谁改了方案，大家都装没看见。我刚准备实话实说，同事就把我拉出去[MASK902]。结果回去一圈发言，时间线突然都一致了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The boss suddenly asked who changed the proposal last night, and everyone acted like they saw nothing. I was just about to tell the truth when my coworker pulled me outside to get our stories straight. When we went back in, everyone’s timeline suddenly matched.

definition_tar_lang: To introduce a safer, softer topic before bringing up the real issue you actually want to discuss. It describes conversational cushioning used to reduce resistance.
sentence_in_context: 他一上来先聊福利待遇，明显是在给后面的加薪请求[MASK903]。
sentence_in_context_gloss: He started by talking about benefits and compensation, obviously cushioning the conversation for the salary raise request that would come later.
paragraph_in_context: 昨晚和室友聊搬家的事，她先问我最近通勤累不累，又说这房子采光一般。我还以为她只是随口吐槽，结果下一句就提想提前退租。原来前面那几句都是在[MASK903]。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night my roommate talked to me about moving. She first asked whether my commute had been tiring lately, then said the apartment's lighting wasn't great. I thought she was just casually complaining, but the next thing she said was that she wanted to end the lease early. Turns out those earlier lines were all cushioning for the real topic.

definition_tar_lang: To split one personal story into multiple posts, clips, or updates so it lasts longer and gets repeated attention. The point is not lying, but portioning out the same material for maximum engagement.
sentence_in_context: 这瓜都嚼三天了，别再[MASK904]吊大家胃口。
sentence_in_context_gloss: We’ve been chewing on this drama for three days already—stop dragging it out bit by bit to keep everyone hooked.
paragraph_in_context: 她昨晚先发一张医院手环，今天又补聊天记录，评论区全在追更。明明一条能说完的事，偏要[MASK904]发成连续剧。我不是不信她，就是看着太会拿捏节奏了。
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Last night she posted a photo of a hospital wristband, and today she added chat screenshots, so everyone in the comments is waiting for the next update. It was obviously something that could’ve been told in one post, but she insisted on splitting it up like a serial drama. It’s not that I don’t believe her—I just feel she really knows how to control the pacing.

definition_tar_lang: To hold onto a tiny piece of private comfort, like a message, photo, or compliment, and revisit it quietly for emotional warmth. It suggests low-key self-soothing rather than public display.
sentence_in_context: 昨晚那句晚安我又翻出来[MASK905]了，真的很顶。
sentence_in_context_gloss: I dug out that goodnight message from last night and held onto it again for comfort—it really hits.
paragraph_in_context: 今天通勤又被客户气到，差点当场破防。午休时翻到她上周随手拍给我的那张晚霞，瞬间缓过来。果然人一累就会开始[MASK905]，靠一点点甜撑完整天。也没想发圈，自己偷着开心就够了。
